title: ₹60 Ka Milk Packet: Farmer, Amul, Retailer – Kisko Kitna?
description: The Amul IPO reel and two Amul franchise reels all pulled strong numbers (the Amul/Fortuner reel hit 21.7M). The audience clearly wants to know who really earns in the Amul system, and our covered Amul reel only touches the parlour's commission.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: Where the ₹60 milk packet's money goes (Amul / GCMMF)
Research date: 3 Nov 2026. Prices and figures are from India, mostly 2025–26.

**HEADLINE FINDING**
- Amul says nearly 80 paise of every rupee consumers pay goes directly to farmers. Amul said nearly 80 paise of every rupee paid by consumers goes directly to farmers. [https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/news/story/amul-mother-dairy-raise-milk-prices-by-rs-2-per-litre-from-may-14-check-new-rates-here-531378-2026-05-14]
- Caveat: this is a company claim covering "milk and milk products", not one packet. GCMMF says it passes almost 80 paise of every rupee paid for milk and milk products to producers. [https://www.newkerala.com/news/a/milk-prices-impacted-monthly-budgets-amul-raises-milk-320.htm]
- Other sources quote 80–85 paise, but these are secondary sites. One says Amul and other coops return 80-85% of the consumer price to farmers. [https://www.shunya.live/farmer-earnings-milk-vs-vegetable-in-india/]
- Mother Dairy, a comparison point, says it passes on approximately 75 to 80% of its milk sales realisation to farmers. [https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/news/story/amul-mother-dairy-raise-milk-prices-by-rs-2-per-litre-from-may-14-check-new-rates-here-531378-2026-05-14]

**THE ₹60 PACKET: WALK-THROUGH**
- The ₹60 is a round-number stand-in. Real Amul 1-litre prices after the 14 May 2026 hike vary by variant and city:
  - Taaza 1 litre went from ₹55 to ₹57. [https://www.zeebiz.com/india/news-amul-milk-price-hike-by-rs-2-per-litre-applicable-from-may-13-dairy-expensive-395451/amp]
  - Shakti 1 litre is ₹64. [https://myojasupdate.net/amul-milk-price-hike-2026/]
  - Mother Dairy toned pouched milk went from ₹58 to ₹60 per litre (Delhi-NCR). [https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/news/story/amul-mother-dairy-raise-milk-prices-by-rs-2-per-litre-from-may-14-check-new-rates-here-531378-2026-05-14]
- SCRIPT MATH (my arithmetic on the sourced percentages, not sourced numbers):
  - Farmer side: ₹60 × 80 paise = ₹48 (Amul's claim above).
  - Retailer: ₹60 × 2.5% = ₹1.50. The 2.5% pouch-milk margin is cited below.
  - Everything else shares the remaining ₹12: village society, union processing and packaging, federation marketing, distributor, retailer, transport.
- STEP 1, Farmer. Procurement is priced per kg of fat.
  - GCMMF raised the farmer procurement price by ₹30 per kg of fat in May 2026, a 3.7% rise over May 2025. [https://dairynews.today/news/amul-increases-milk-prices-across-india-due-to-rising-costs.html]
  - Dudhsagar Dairy (an Amul member union) raised its price to ₹855 per kg fat from 1 June. [https://www.indiancooperative.com/co-op-news-snippets/dudhsagar-hikes-procurement-price-by-rs-25-per-kg-fat/]
  - A weaker secondary source puts per-litre rates at buffalo ₹54.05–₹63.06 and cow ₹36.68–₹38.68 (June 2026). Amul currently procures buffalo milk at ₹54.05–₹63.06 per litre and cow milk at ₹36.68–₹38.68 per litre. [https://www.agrijob.in/amul-dairy-cooperative-registration-milk-rate-income-guide/]
  - Older data point: farmers got ₹36.6 per litre on average (Scroll, about 2017). [https://scroll.in/article/858576/the-amul-story-how-politics-is-hurting-the-economics-of-gujarats-milk-cooperatives]
  - Amul pays 15–20% more than private dairies, per one case study. Amul procures milk at a rate 15–20% higher than private dairies and 5–7% higher than other cooperatives. [https://doughnuteconomics.org/stories/amul-doughnut-design-case-study-9554cada-3890-4247-89e1-ae06c2a7355f]
- STEP 2, Village cooperative society.
  - Each society pays its staff from a margin of 2–4% on every litre sold to the district union. The staff are an accountant, milk collector, milk tester and administrator. (Forbes India, 2015, so dated.) [https://www.forbesindia.com/article/leadership-awards-2015/cow-to-consumer-beyond-profit-for-gujarat-cooperative-milk-marketing-federation/41207/1]
  - The society has its own balance sheet, and its committee works in an honorary capacity. [https://www.forbesindia.com/article/leadership-awards-2015/cow-to-consumer-beyond-profit-for-gujarat-cooperative-milk-marketing-federation/41207/1]
  - At year-end, part of the society's profit pays each member a patronage bonus based on the quantity of milk poured. [https://dudhsagardairy.coop/about-us/amul-pattern/]
- STEP 3, District union. Example: Dudhsagar, Mehsana.
  - It had a turnover of about ₹9,043 crore in FY2025-26 and procured over 36.34 lakh litres per day. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dudhsagar_Dairy]
  - Milk is bought from village societies at provisional prices through the year, and most of the surplus pool price goes to farmers at year-end. [https://www.icra.in/Rating/GetRationalReportFilePdf?id=134662]
- STEP 4, Federation (GCMMF), the surprise.
  - FY23 revenue was ₹55,125 crore, with profit after tax of ₹82 crore and a PAT margin of 0.15%. [https://www.crisilratings.com/mnt/winshare/Ratings/RatingList/RatingDocs/GujaratCo_OperativeMilkMarketingFederationLimited_April%2030_%202024_RR_341440.html]
  - So the federation's profit margin (0.15%) is far below the retailer's 2.5% margin on pouch milk.
  - The federation distributes excess funds to unions after meeting working capital and capex needs. [same CRISIL link]
  - Scale: GCMMF revenue rose 11% to ₹65,911 crore in FY2024-25. [https://agronfoodprocessing.com/amuls-fy25-revenue-surges-12-to-%E2%82%B990000-crore-gcmmf-turnover-grows-11/]
  - The Amul brand's turnover in FY2025-26 rose 11%, passing ₹1 lakh crore. [https://dairynews.today/news/amul-increases-milk-prices-across-india-due-to-rising-costs.html]
- STEP 5, Distributor.
  - Liquid milk margin is 2.5–3.5% for the distributor, per a distributorship guide (secondary source). The same table lists ₹1–2 per litre on an MRP basis. Liquid milk (pouch): distributor 2.5–3.5%, retailer 3–5%, ₹1–2 per litre. [https://spirestock.com/blog/amul-distributorship-india-cost-margin-process]
  - Illustration from the same source: a distributor selling 1,000 litres daily at ₹1.5
